name: Popliteus tendon
description: Intracapsular, extrasynovial tendon from the popliteal sulcus on the lateral femoral condyle, below the LCL origin, through the popliteal hiatus to its muscle behind the tibia. A low-signal band about 3–4 mm thick (thinner in women), often outlined by recess fluid.

normal_values.origin_vs_lcl_origin: 17–19 mm distal and anterior in Western and Indian series; about 9 mm, mostly directly below, in a Korean series

variants_pitfalls: Fluid around the tendon down to about 2 cm below the lateral plateau is the subpopliteal recess, not a tear. A tear needs discontinuity, retraction or an empty sulcus; fluid behind the tendon outside the recess suggests a capsular tear.

Its fluid-filled sheath crossing the lateral meniscus posterior horn mimics a peripheral tear on far lateral sagittal images (27.5% in one series); follow it onto the tendon. A second band parallel to it in the hiatus is a displaced meniscal flap.
Most popliteus injuries are muscular and fewer than 10% are isolated; tendon tears are often femoral avulsions (empty sulcus), so check the LCL, popliteofibular ligament and PCL.
A cyamella (sesamoid, about 0.6–1.8%) is a corticated ossicle, not a loose body or avulsion.
